sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events E0–E2535. The transcript contains transcription errors and several events spanning speaker changes; these are marked U where mixed attribution cannot be separated at event level. No edited teaser replay was identifiable. Personal histories directly explaining worldview development were retained as substantive answers. No unsupported slogan was confirmed; one possible protective non-slogan episode remains uncertain.

candidates.speaker: B
candidates.quote: God could create whatever Universe he wanted to
candidates.explanation: Unrestricted divine choice could neutralize Carroll's expectation-based objection about absent scientific revelation (E417–471), without explaining why this pattern was chosen. However, Halvorson acknowledges continuing difficulty (E472–479), offers discovery and freedom as reasons (E505–530), and uses omnipotence to motivate empirical inquiry. Whether this excludes contrary evidence regardless of merits remains unclear.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: we don't know if those rules are true it's very speculative physics
contrasts.explanation: The rejection of multiverse extravagance has supporting reasons: independently motivated theories can generate many universes from simple rules (E719–737). Carroll expressly qualifies their truth and makes the fine-tuning application conditional (E737–745).

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: God builds the Target right God makes the laws of physics
contrasts.explanation: The memorable phrase summarizes a conditional objection to a design argument Halvorson otherwise favors: a creator of physical laws would also determine the possibilities and their probabilities (E854–866). It challenges the dartboard analogy rather than supplying unsupported proof of God.
